title: Intermittent checkout saturation during a regional rollout

evidence.text: At 14:02 UTC, checkout p95 latency in region east rose from 0.9 seconds to 4.8 seconds; west remained near 0.9 seconds. The rate of original client checkout submissions was flat in both regions.
At 13:58 UTC, the east proxy fleet completed a policy rollout that reduced its upstream timeout from 2 seconds to 700 milliseconds and increased its retry limit from one attempt to three.

A gateway application release completed in both east and west at 13:54 UTC. All old-version pods were removed before the incident, and no application rollback or mixed-version comparison was performed.

For 41 reconstructed east checkout requests, proxy access records contain the same client operation identifier at approximately 0, 0.7, and 1.4 seconds. The gateway assigned a distinct server request identifier to each arrival.
Between 14:02 and 14:20 UTC, east gateway arrivals and active workers increased to 3.1 times baseline while original client submissions stayed flat. CPU throttling began after active workers doubled.
The database audit stream, which independently records every failover and rejected transaction and had no ingestion gaps that day, records neither event in east from 13:30 through 15:00 UTC.

Database execution-time p95 stayed between 110 and 125 milliseconds in both regions. Several gateway log lines say 'db timeout', but their structured field identifies a gateway connection-pool acquisition timeout before any database session was opened.

The payment dashboard shows zero failed payment calls in east during the incident. Its denominator includes only calls for which an HTTP response was received; attempts abandoned by the caller before a response are not counted.

Packet capture was not enabled, and east egress flow logs for 13:50 through 14:30 UTC were not retained. No source independently records whether response-less payment attempts reached the payment network.

The east telemetry collector reported a full queue and dropped 18 percent of gateway span batches from 14:05 through 14:17 UTC. Collector counters do not identify which request outcomes were in the dropped batches.

The retained trace set contains no payment spans longer than 700 milliseconds. Trace export occurs when a span closes; a gateway worker killed at its deadline does not close or export its active child span.
At 14:21 UTC, operators restored the east proxy policy to a 2-second timeout and one attempt. No application, database, or payment-network change was made during the mitigation window.
New repeated operation identifiers fell to baseline within two minutes of the proxy rollback. Active workers, CPU throttling, and checkout p95 returned to baseline over the following seven minutes.
A certificate-expiry warning fired at 14:01 UTC for an unused staging hostname. Production certificate inventory shows the east gateway certificate valid for another 74 days.

The product-catalog cache in east evicted 22 percent more entries than usual at 13:57 UTC. Checkout request reconstruction shows catalog lookup completed before the timed portion of all 41 reconstructed operations.

A DNS monitor reported one failed probe from a west-region probe host at 14:06 UTC. East proxy resolver metrics show successful production-name resolution throughout, but per-request DNS packets were not captured.

hypotheses.text: The gateway application release was a necessary cause of the east checkout degradation.
An orders-database failover or transaction-rejection episode initiated the east checkout degradation.
A payment-network slowdown contributed to the response-less payment attempts during the east incident.
The east proxy retry policy amplified gateway load and prolonged checkout latency.
The telemetry collector discarded at least one span batch containing a response-less payment attempt.

edges.relation: The deployed timeout and retry settings generated repeated gateway arrivals for single client operations.
Repeated arrivals increased worker concurrency until CPU throttling occurred.
A database failover caused the logged connection-pool acquisition timeouts.
Payment-network response time exceeded the proxy deadline for some attempts.
The retained telemetry establishes that no payment attempt exceeded 700 milliseconds.
Restoring the prior proxy settings removed retry amplification before gateway saturation subsided.
Gateway pool exhaustion prevented some logged requests from opening database sessions.
Collector queue loss selectively removed the slowest gateway outcomes from retained traces.

actions.text: Keep the restored proxy policy in east while monitoring repeated operation identifiers and worker concurrency.
Force an orders-database failover in east before changing gateway traffic levels.
Capture deadline outcomes and egress timing in a bounded canary before deciding whether the payment network contributed.
Restore the three-attempt, 700-millisecond proxy policy because the payment dashboard reports no failures.
Preserve the current application version while running a controlled single-variable comparison against the prior version.
Increase telemetry queue capacity and add counters for deadline-abandoned child spans.
